targets.text: PR fixer escalation: within one story, a try that does not pass is retried by a stronger fixer (Qwen, then Codex), each try reviewed by a different model, and an unavailable level falls through instead of stalling
No try's commit is ever reviewed by the actor or backend that wrote it, enforced at the verdict step from the store, not from routing
A level that is unavailable never stalls a story: it falls through or hands back once within the 3-try budget
Authors of PRs in vars.fixer_repos whose PR the fixer works on, and the operator who watches the fixer's stories
PR authors see one status comment per story naming each try's level and fixer, and at most one hand-back
Every try of a story uses qwen-fixer on spark2 and every review uses codex-reviewer; a PR Qwen cannot fix burns all 3 tries on the same model and hands back
Today every try of the 2026-10-10 stories ran on qwen-fixer and was reviewed by codex-reviewer (live runs)

Try 1 is fixed by qwen-fixer and reviewed by codex-reviewer; try 2 by codex-fixer (Codex on spark, its commit carried to spark2's gate) and reviewed by qwen-reviewer; try 3 by the next enabled level; the status comment names the level and the fixer of each try
A story's try 2 is dispatched to codex-fixer and its commit is reviewed by qwen-reviewer, both from the store's records, not routing hints
A second model often fixes what the first could not; escalating within the 3-try budget raises the fix rate without more tries or more cost on easy PRs
Escalation never adds a try: the 3-try budget per story is unchanged

A shared variable fixer_levels lists the levels in order, each {level, actor, reviewer, pool, queue, enabled}, plus fixer_unavailable (next or hand_back); it can only choose among agent and review steps that exist in the trusted workflows
Changing fixer_levels cannot run an actor or workflow that is not in the trusted pr-fix and review-commit; a level naming an unknown step fails closed

queue.progress resolves a request's level at dispatch from its try (the key's count plus one), skipping a level that is unavailable (actor disabled or deleted, its pool over budget, or a capacity_exhausted cooldown) as fixer_unavailable says, and writes fixer, reviewer, level and attempt into the dispatch event; each level has its own queue and pool (pr-fixer on qwen-spark2, pr-fixer-codex on codex-spark), and queue.stop covers every queue
Each level's queue is first come, first served on its own pool, so a busy Qwen never delays a Codex try; /stop removes a story's request from every queue

pr-fix stays one workflow: one agent step per level guarded by when fixer == <actor>, a Codex hand-off that exports the fixer's commits (start..head, size-capped) from spark into the store and imports them into a fixer-owned worktree on spark2, then the single gate unchanged; new ROLE_FIX digest (the old one kept while its runs may still push)
The gate still judges the exact commit the Codex fixer made (same SHA after the hand-off); an export over the size cap fails the try with a clear code and the story goes on

review-commit runs one review step per reviewer guarded by when reviewer == <actor>; the verdict step takes the single review step that succeeded and still derives reviewer and implementer from the store (never the same actor or backend, read-only, trusted digest); REVIEWER_BACKENDS gains qwen; a qwen-reviewer actor digest is pinned; new ROLE_REVIEW digest
codex-reviewer never reviews a Codex try and qwen-reviewer never reviews a Qwen try; the verdict step refuses otherwise
A Codex try that fails with capacity_exhausted records a cooldown for its level and the story goes on at the next level (the try counts toward the 3)
After capacity_exhausted the level is skipped until its cooldown ends, and the try that hit it counts toward the 3
The fixer still never pushes or merges; only publish-fix pushes as the App, from spark2; a mis-routed level fails closed at the verdict step
No new code path pushes; publish-fix's push placement and trust checks are unchanged
A live story whose Qwen try does not pass is retried by Codex, reviewed by Qwen, and either published or handed back once, with the status comment naming both levels
The status comment of that live story names Qwen for try 1 and Codex for try 2

tasks.summary: Levels: fixer_levels and per-level queues resolved at dispatch
acceptance_criteria: A shared variable fixer_levels (ordered {level, actor, reviewer, pool, queue, enabled}) and fixer_unavailable (next|hand_back) are seeded in variables.json; level 1 is qwen-fixer/codex-reviewer/qwen-spark2/pr-fixer

queue.progress computes the try as the key's count plus one at dispatch, picks that try's level, skips a level whose actor is disabled or deleted, whose pool is over budget or which is in a capacity cooldown, and writes fixer, reviewer, level and attempt into the dispatch event; with no level left it hands back once (fixer_unavailable hand_back) or keeps waiting never; a story never gets a 4th try

Each level's queue is its own queue document on its own pool, first come first served; queue.add routes a retry to its next level's queue; queue.stop and the dispatch rule cover every queue in fixer_levels
tasks.instruction: culture_rules/node/actions/queue.py (_admission/_dispatch), queue-add/queue-progress/queue-stop workflows, pr-fixer-dispatch condition data.queue in vars; reuse limits.pool_cap and engine.claims key_state

acceptance_criteria: A try whose agent step fails capacity_exhausted records a cooldown for its level (default 1 h, variable fixer_capacity_cooldown_s) and the story's retry goes to the next level; the failed try counts toward the 3
tasks.instruction: Extend pr-fixer-retry-failed's match or add pr-fixer-retry-capacity; the cooldown lives in actor_usage or a small store document read by queue.progress

tasks.summary: Codex hand-off: export on spark, import on spark2
acceptance_criteria: Built-in handoff.export (placed on spark) packs start_sha..head_after from the Codex fixer's worktree through a run-as seam, refuses over a size cap (handoff_too_large) and stores it in a handoffs collection; handoff.import (placed on spark2) fetches the base as culture-fixer, indexes the pack with --fix-thin and creates a fixer-owned worktree whose HEAD is exactly head_after
Tests prove the gate judges the same SHA the fixer made, a pack over the cap fails the try with handoff_too_large, and a corrupt pack fails closed
tasks.instruction: Model on gate.py _import (pack-objects/index-pack --strict) and its run-as seam; never ssh; the pack stays well under Mongo's 16 MB

tasks.summary: pr-fix: one agent step per level plus the hand-off
acceptance_criteria: pr-fix's fix body runs agent_qwen (when fixer == qwen-fixer) or agent_codex then handoff export/import (when fixer == codex-fixer), then the single gate fed from one source step; outputs implementer and reviewer; pr-fixer-dispatch maps fixer, reviewer and attempt; new ROLE_FIX digest added, old kept
The status comment names each try's level and fixer (fixer_status takes the agent step that ran, not the first); one hand-back per story
No new code path pushes: publish-fix and its placement and trust checks are unchanged (bundle test)
tasks.instruction: Keep lineage.final_gate's single-gate rule; avoid two edges into one port (last edge wins)

tasks.summary: review-commit: the reviewer follows the fixer
acceptance_criteria: review-commit runs review_codex (when reviewer == codex-reviewer) or review_qwen (when reviewer == qwen-reviewer); the verdict step reads review_steps, takes the one that succeeded and still derives reviewer and implementer from the store, refusing the same actor or backend; REVIEWER_BACKENDS gains qwen
A qwen-reviewer actor (read-only, plan mode, pool qwen-spark2) is added to docs/rules/pr-fixer/actors and its digest pinned in TRUSTED_ACTOR_DIGESTS; new ROLE_REVIEW digest, old kept

tasks.summary: Actors, docs and the operator's setup
acceptance_criteria: codex-fixer actor JSON (machine spark, pool codex-spark, max_concurrency 1, workspace-write) in the bundle; docs/operations/pr-fixer.md documents the levels, the hand-off, the reviewer rule, and the operator's setup: the culture-codex-fixer account, its codex login, the second Codex bridge, grant secrets and the sudoers entry; the rollout lists new rules, variables and digests; CHANGELOG and version bump
tasks.instruction: No secret values; grant names only

tasks.summary: A live story escalates from Qwen to Codex
acceptance_criteria: After the operator's setup and rollout, a live story whose Qwen try does not pass gets a Codex try reviewed by Qwen and is published or handed back once; its status comment names Qwen for try 1 and Codex for try 2
tasks.instruction: Operator-run setup and rollout; Claude watches the story and files the evidence
